title: Frustrated
author: Dramatic_Wheel2416
selftext: It's so frustrating the ridicule that comes with using AI. People need to understand,  it's a tool. They're either going to have to adapt...  or not. And I completely get it... it would be devastating if something I had spent years studying was suddenly made simple for everyone but, that doesn't give anyone the right to ridicule anyone else. I'm the single mother of a 5 year old, if I find something I'm decent at that I enjoy,  who are you to tell me it's wrong? Also,  I've learned more about actually coding in the past couple months with Ai than I previously had in all my 38 years. It's a tool, not a replacement.

I think their ideals and visions are also getting replaced; it used to be that devs need to study hard and grind for X years to "get good." That is not really true anymore. comments.author: Tenthul
comments.body:
It's ok to use a new tool, but be aware of the cost it brings us as society as well. Everybody gets a new tool, great. But also it's bringing insane layoffs, completely upending how things are done, potentially destroying the economy, the environment (and our electric bills in the process), peoples sanity (who don't understand how to use it), our privacy and who the hell knows what else how the government and private organizations will use it. The dangers personally to deep fakes, the enhancement capabilities to propaganda and scammers.

It's a great tool if you understand it, but don't sweep all the bad and bad potential under the rug. We're paying for all this in a wide varieties of ways, and we shouldn't hamstring ourselves by not using it at this point, but we should all wish for Pandora's Box to close itself. Our individual little gains out of it will almost certainly not outweigh the negatives it will bring to society at large.

But are we going to be ones to make the difference? Just like our individual contribution to water waste and pollution where corporations contribute 80%-whatever, no, so don't hold yourself back either. 

But don't write off the very real problems that all this brings along with it. And that's where a lot of people's anger towards AI comes from, it's not all just about generated AI art.

comments.author: karlmillsom
comments.body:
I see a lot of the argument coming from the perspective of video games as art. And that then emphasises the value of purity. And I absolutely consider some video games art.

But they also have a function. That function is to be played. And if players have a great time playing a game, then its provenance doesn’t matter so much. 

I think in that case, the dev shouldn’t be winning “best art style” awards for the game, or whatever, but that’s obviously not why that dev got into it. 

By way of analogy, not all drawings are art. Some people make drawings for instruction manuals for kitchen appliances. If somebody used AI to help them in that job, it would be pretty absurd to accuse them of harming the art world. Their drawings have a function, which is to help people understand the appliance they just bought. They don’t exist to be appreciate as an expression of the artist’s creativity. 

With video games, it’s tough because they absolutely can sit in that camp and be truly stunning works of art (and that’s not just purely about art style and aesthetic, it can be innovative mechanics, elegant level design, etc. ). But not all games are that. 

It’s also tough because, despite all that I’ve just said, AI SLOP is a real problem. The extreme end of the scale is people trying to make a quick buck by one-shot prompting any old crap and throwing it on Steam with no care for the player at all. 

But if a dev uses AI meticulously to produce a game that they have taken care over to create a genuine experience for the player, then that’s simply not the same thing.

comments.author: nvidiastock

No one serious is worried about being replaced by whatever slop most people make with AI; what they're upset about is that platforms are being flooded with very low quality content. No one in the world outside of your family cares if you are a single mother, disabled vet or whatever; what they care about is the quality of your PRODUCT. 

If you went to the store to buy some fruit and the fruit was rotten, you made a complaint and then the manager would rant on the internet about all these people "scared that rotten fruit are replacing ripe fruit", how would you feel about that? That's what you're doing right now. The issue is not whatever you used, it's the fact that it's obvious that you used AI by the fact that your product is very very bad.

If you make a professional level game with AI, most people won't care because 99% won't be able to tell. The biggest tell for using AI is low effort / bad game. Stop making bad games. You'll do much better.
